idea.title: 5 messages for a buyer who went quiet
idea.hook: Copy these 5 messages for a buyer who went quiet

slides.heading: Copy these 5 messages for a buyer who went **quiet**
slides.body: Day 1 to day 30. Paste them straight into WhatsApp.

slides.heading: They asked for details. Then **silence.**
slides.body: You sent photos and the price of the 3-bedroom in East Legon. Two blue ticks, no reply. Most agents send one 'hello?' and give up. Use these instead, one at a time.

slides.heading: "Hi Kofi, did the photos come through okay? Happy to send a short video of the place if that helps."
slides.body: Easy to answer, no pressure, and it shows you're paying attention.

slides.heading: "Quick one: is the budget still around the same, or should I look at other options for you?"
slides.body: Gives them a reason to reply even if this house isn't it.

slides.heading: "I'm showing the place on Saturday morning. Want me to hold a slot for you?"
slides.body: A real day and time makes it much easier to say yes.

slides.heading: "A similar unit just came in nearby. Want me to send it over?"
slides.body: A new listing gives you a fresh reason to start talking again.

slides.heading: "Should I close your file for now? No problem either way, just tell me."
slides.body: People often reply to this one, even if only to say 'not yet'.

slides.heading: Make them **land**
Save this so you have the words **next time**

caption:
Copy these 5 messages for a buyer who went quiet.

A lead who stops replying isn't always a lost lead.
Most of the time they got busy, not uninterested.
Space your follow-ups out: day 1, 3, 7, 14 and 30.
Each message gives them an easy reason to reply.
The day 30 one gets people talking, even if it's 'not yet'.

idea.title: When a client says 'the price is too high'
idea.angle: Replies that handle the objection without discounting first
idea.hook: Steal these replies for 'the price is too high'

slides.heading: Steal these replies for '**the price is too high**'
slides.body: Before you rush to offer a discount.

slides.heading: The buyer says it's **too expensive**
slides.body: Your first thought is to call the landlord and ask for less. Wait. 'Too high' usually means 'I'm not sure it's worth it' or 'it's above my budget'. Find out which one first.

slides.heading: "I hear you. Too high compared to what? Another place you've seen, or your budget?"
slides.body: One question, and now you know what you're really dealing with.

slides.heading: "Can you send me that one? Let me compare them side by side for you."
slides.body: Often the 'cheaper' one has no parking, no water tank or is further out.

slides.heading: "What monthly or total amount works for you? I'll show you the best I have at that price."
slides.body: You keep the client, even if not on this house.

slides.heading: "If the price was right, is this the one? Then let me see what I can do."
slides.body: Only start negotiating once they've said yes to the property itself.

slides.heading: Don't **discount first**
bullets: Get a yes on the property first

slides.heading: Save this for the next **price objection**

caption:
Steal these replies for 'the price is too high'.

'Too high' doesn't always mean 'give me a discount'.
Sometimes it means 'I saw something cheaper'.
Sometimes it means 'this is above my budget'.
Ask one question first, then reply to the real problem.
Negotiate only once they've said yes to the property.

idea.title: When your AI assistant should hand over to you
idea.angle: Smart human handoff: the moments a real agent must step in
idea.hook: The 7 moments your AI assistant should hand the chat to you

slides.heading: 7 moments your AI assistant should hand the chat **to you**
slides.body: A good system knows when to step back.

slides.heading: AI can answer fast. It **can't close** for you.
slides.body: A chatbot can reply at midnight and ask about budget. But some moments need a real agent. The system has to be built to spot them, not left to guess.

slides.heading: The buyer is **ready**
bullets: They ask to negotiate the price
They want to pay a deposit
They ask about documents or land title
They say 'can I talk to someone?'

slides.heading: Things get **sensitive**
bullets: The client sounds upset or confused
The question isn't in your listings or FAQs
It's a big buyer, like a diaspora client buying in Lekki

slides.heading: "Good question. Let me get Ama, our agent, to answer you directly. She'll message you shortly."
slides.body: Honest, warm, and it tells them a real person is coming.

slides.heading: "Hi, Ama here. I've read your chat, so no need to repeat yourself. About the deposit..."
slides.body: Pick up exactly where the AI stopped. Never make them start over.

slides.heading: It's the **system**, not the tool
slides.body: AI isn't smart on its own. Handoff rules, your listings and clear prompts make it work. That's how we build Kortexa: the AI does the fast part, you do the human part.

slides.heading: Save this before you set up **any chatbot**

caption:
7 moments your AI assistant should hand the chat to you.

An AI assistant is great for fast replies and basic questions.
But negotiations, deposits and land title questions need you.
So do upset clients and anything outside your listings.
A good system spots these moments and passes the chat on cleanly.
A bad one keeps talking and loses the client.

idea.title: The enquiry you saw at 11pm
idea.angle: What happens to late-night messages and a better way to handle them
idea.hook: What to text the lead who messaged you at 11pm

slides.heading: What to text the lead who messaged you **at 11pm**
slides.body: Because 'I'll reply in the morning' is where leads go to die.

slides.heading: You saw it. You said **'tomorrow'.**
slides.body: An Instagram DM at 11pm: 'Is the 2-bedroom in Ikeja still available?' You're tired, so you leave it. By morning they've asked three other agents, and one replied.

slides.heading: "Yes, it's available! I'll send full details and photos first thing tomorrow. When's a good time to call?"
slides.body: Ten seconds. They know you're real and you're on it.

slides.heading: "Good morning! Here are the photos. Rent is yearly. Would you like to view it this week?"
slides.body: Photos, the key details and one clear next step: a viewing.

slides.heading: "So sorry for the late reply! Is the 2-bedroom still what you need? I can show it today."
slides.body: Own it, skip the excuses, and give them a reason to reply.

slides.heading: Don't rely on **memory**
bullets: Save the 11pm reply as a WhatsApp quick reply
Mark late messages unread so you see them
Keep photos for each listing in one folder
Or let a system reply instantly for you

slides.heading: Save this for your **next late-night** lead

caption:
What to text the lead who messaged you at 11pm.

Late-night messages are some of the easiest leads to lose.
You see them, you plan to reply in the morning, and by then they've moved on.
A 10-second reply tonight keeps you in the game.
A proper follow-up at 8am moves them to a viewing.
If you missed it, say sorry and offer a viewing straight away.
